identity: University of Amsterdam BSc Sociology, ordinary full-time English pathway, 2026–2027, recognised programme 56601; bilingual pathway has same course content.
controllingSource: Current dated programme 5890/41082, elective page 40601, transition/progression 40602 and twenty-four individual course entries. Together sufficient; no unresolved formal conflict requires redundant OER research.
components: Reading and sociological reasoning prepare for Sociology as Craft 2, which develops the academic literature review and writing.
Introduction to Sociology: Concepts, Issues and Research
Introduces quantitative, qualitative and mixed research and hands-on surveys; the collected data are used in Introduction to Statistics.

A short intensive qualitative project uses observation and interviewing, research ethics and a student-conference presentation. Prior participation in Social Research Methodology is strongly recommended.
Ordinary second-year progression requires 42 first-year Sociology credits. The domain examines how schooling and work reproduce or challenge inequalities.
Race, Gender, and Sexuality in Times of Fascism
Requires 42 first-year Sociology credits. Studies intersecting race, gender and sexuality through epistemology, political economy and contemporary fascist forces.
Requires 42 first-year Sociology credits. Examines migration, citizenship and political, structural, social and cultural integration.
Requires 42 first-year Sociology credits. Examines urban social theory, political economy, planning debates, postcolonial critique and urban inequality.
Complete 42 first-year Sociology credits, including Introduction to Statistics, before Advanced Statistics. Multiple regression is taught through software-based analysis.
Requires 42 first-year Sociology credits and introductory statistics and quantitative research methods. Studies population health, social determinants and health inequalities.
Sociological Theory 3: Society, Social Action and Inequality
Requires 42 first-year Sociology credits. Compares macro- and micro-level accounts of social action and inequality.
Requires 42 first-year Sociology credits. Studies cultural globalisation, colonial power, oppression and transnational resistance.
Requires 42 first-year Sociology credits. Studies how cultural meanings and social structures interact in contemporary theory.
Complete 42 first-year Sociology credits, including the Amsterdam Research Project. Develops coding, thematic and discourse analysis and reflexive qualitative inquiry.

Thirty credits remain genuinely open for eligible electives, a minor, study abroad or a combination including an optional internship. Check each chosen course’s level, entry conditions and registration. No particular package or internship is compulsory.
Complete 60 Sociology credits including Advanced Statistics. Develops the epistemological and practical integration of qualitative and quantitative methods, alongside the final research project.
Complete 60 Sociology credits. Studies the institutional, political and social processes of policy development, implementation and evaluation.

Before this eighteen-credit project starts, at least 108 first- and second-year Sociology credits must be completed and registered, including Advanced Statistics and Qualitative Analysis. Small-group supervision and feedback support an individual bachelor thesis covering the empirical research cycle. Select a project from the offered research groups; no particular topic is guaranteed.

findings: The two public pages and dated catalogue confirm 180 credits, full-time Sociology, RIO56601 and English/bilingual variants with the same content. Choose the existing English pathway rather than invent a specialisation. Curriculum instructionLanguages metadata says DUTCH but the official English pathway and each bilingual course’s language arrangements confirm its availability; it is not a competing academic route. No track-dependent credit choice is needed.

The dated curriculum and transition table explicitly replace Introduction to Sociology: Concepts, Issues and Research, Sociological Theory 2: Critical Theory, Race/Gender/Sexuality in Times of Fascism and Urban Society. Historical predecessor names are corrected without stacking replacement credits. First year eleven units60, second year ten units60, third year open30 plus Mixed Methods6, Public Policy6 and Bachelor Research18:25components180unique credits.

The four pillars are theory, empirical science, methodology and sociological craftsmanship. Theory1 studies interactions/order; Theory2 Marx/Frankfurt critical theory; Theory3 macro/micro accounts of social action and inequality; Theory4 cultural meanings and structural organisation, including Bourdieu and related theorists. All six second-year domains remain compulsory: education/work, race/gender/sexuality, migration/citizenship, urban society, health/society and globalising cultures.

The first-year survey-methodology data feed the introductory statistics course; the Amsterdam project is a short observation/interview study with ethics and a conference presentation. Craft1 prepares reading/reasoning for Craft2’s literature review and academic writing. Evolution uses cultural evolution and complexity; Philosophy covers ontology, epistemology, context and ethics. No invented specialist pathway or extra credit is added.

Ordinary second-year admission is42 completed first-year Sociology credits. Advanced Statistics also requires Intro Statistics passed; Qualitative Analysis also requires Amsterdam Research Project passed. Health/Society explicitly requires introductory statistics and quantitative methods. Completing ordinary year one60 satisfies these. Qualitative Analysis includes positionality, coding, thematic and discourse analysis. Advanced Statistics centres multiple regression. Non-Sociology minor/exchange requirements do not replace the actual Sociology pathway requirements.

Mixed Methods requires60 Sociology credits including Advanced Statistics. It develops epistemological/practical integration of qualitative and quantitative designs and data, serving as a bridge to the final research. Public Policy needs60 Sociology credits and examines policy framing, formulation, implementation and institutional/power contexts across several domains. They run alongside final research in semester6, not a fabricated prior-completion gate.

The final18-credit research project requires108 credits from the first/second-year Sociology curriculum, completed and registered before its start, specifically including Advanced Statistics and Qualitative Analysis. The normal prior120 satisfies it. Small research groups exchange feedback; assessment is the individual bachelor thesis, covering research question/design, data collection or secondary data, analysis, interpretation and reporting. Project topics come from offered research groups; no unverified specific topic, compulsory placement or extra thesis is invented.

The30-credit free-choice semester remains genuinely open. The dated elective page permits free courses, minors, abroad and an optional12-credit internship as part of the space; this is not a mandatory30-credit sociology menu or internship. Each eventual choice must meet entry/level/registration conditions. Optional honours is additional, not counted. The public summary and dated course pages agree on all substantive/formal requirements; no essential evidence remains missing.
